details:
In the EU at least, it's still a valid license condition to revoke a license if an asset is involved with generative AI work. That could mean you no longer have permission to use the asset on VRC, and in cases where that use infringes IP rights, you could potentially use the Digital Services Act to request removal of the infringing content. Many asset licenses prohibit redistribution to third parties, which could include generative AI depending on how it's being used, and a large number of prefabs already explicitly prohibit generative AI use (Which is specifically acknowledged by the DSA). This raises questions about whether worlds using them comply with VRChat's guidelines and upload requirements.

Now that VRChat has publicly acknowledged relationships with long-tenured creators using generative AI and is openly supporting the creation of AI worlds, I think they need to consider the licensing of the assets these creators use. Labels aside, VRChat should update its Community Guidelines and upload consent policy to address these issues. They took a hard stance against ripping for similar reasons, to the point of encrypting the cache, so I don't understand why asset licensing is being treated differently now. I don't want this to become a matter of "our friends are scared to upload" rather than a matter of protecting the community. Ripping and unauthorized use of licensed assets are not identical, but both raise questions about consent and permission. VRChat should clearly state how it intends to uphold asset and prefab licensing restrictions in AI-assisted content.
title: Enforcing Asset Licensing Requirements for AI Assisted Worlds.
